subject: research/robofab-selfparts
professional: a senior robotic assembly-planning researcher (assembly-by-disassembly, non-directional blocking graphs, grasp-aware sequence planning as in Wilson & Latombe 1994 and Tian et al. ASAP 2024); first checks: are the counts right under the stated rules, does the grasp model include the jaw/finger bodies or only floating pads, and does the self-replication question get answered for the design's own jaw

evidence.correctness: All headline counts recomputed by an independent script (/tmp/claude-0/audit-robofab-selfparts/indep.py, no import from the subject) that uses a different method: collision by discrete 0.25 mm translation stepping to 60 mm instead of the subject's analytic half-space test, and support by 0.5 mm grid-sampled contact patches instead of rectangle intersection, brute force over all 720 permutations. Results: free/side 384 at jaw 30 and 40, top 120, all arms 0 at jaw 25 and 29.5 with cover stuck (so the 30.0 mm minimum holds), gravity off 720/720/120, pad_t 2 and 10 both 384. All match experiments/results.txt; experiments/run.py regenerates results.txt byte-identical (diff empty). Also confirmed the '5!: cover must go last' explanation for the top arm (all 120 have cover in position 6). Outputs are right under the model's stated rules.
evidence.completeness: Claimed: 8 tests (8 pass, 1.2 s), experiments/run.py (runs, 1.06 s, output identical to the committed file), sections 1-5 of results.txt, a paper (whitepaper.md, 18 lines), refs.bib, live page (https://marisstella.app/research/robofab-selfparts/ returns 200, title and 384 present). Everything claimed runs end to end. README runtimes (~2 s tests, ~10 s experiments) are stale (1.2 s, 1.1 s); minor.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests: 8 OK. Four seeded mutations via quality_mutate.py, all survived: removing the centre-of-mass support check (headline 384 -> 576), dropping +y/-y from the side arm (384 -> 204), removing both pad collision checks (no change), widening the settle gap to 20 mm. No test pins any headline number (384, 120, 720, 30 mm); test_search_matches_bruteforce compares the DP with a brute force that calls the same moves()/stable(), so it checks the search, not the geometry.
evidence.craft: Read src/robofab_selfparts/model.py (182 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py. Small and readable, standard library only, DP over subsets is correct (brute-force agreement). Defects: ARMS_ALL is defined after the class that uses it (model.py:144, used at :93) and moves() loops all six directions then filters by self.allowed with a linear tuple compare; single-letter names throughout; the pad model (pads(), two checks in moves()) is dead weight in this geometry (removing it changes no output); results.txt is printed by a script with no seed/version header.
evidence.claims: Backed: every count in README bullets 1-3 and the paper abstract (recomputed above); 30.0 mm minimum; limitations section is candid (threshold restates design, free=side is geometry-specific). Not backed or misleading: README bullet 4 says pad thickness changes nothing because 'the pads always find free space'; in fact removing both pad checks entirely changes no count, so the grasp model reduces to a bounding-box width test and the negative result is an artefact of floating pads, not a finding. Motivation (README:20) frames the question as whether the arm's own end effector can grip every part of a copy of itself, but jaw_open is swept independently; the toy gripper's own fingers open 8 mm at rest and at most 12 mm between rails (rails 4..36, fingers 10 wide), far below the 30 mm required, and this answer ('no, under its own design') is never stated. Runtimes stale. Citations openly marked as not re-verified.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: assembly-by-disassembly with directional blocking graphs (Wilson & Latombe 1994, 'Geometric reasoning about mechanical assembly', AIJ; Homem de Mello & Sanderson 1991 AND/OR graphs) and grasp-aware physical-feasibility sequence planning on real meshes (Tian et al. 2024 ASAP, cited). Those already enumerate feasible orders under directional and gravity constraints, with real gripper geometry in ASAP. This project applies the same idea to one 7-box toy and finds the arm must open as wide as the widest part, which the README itself calls a restatement of the design. Not new; the 384-vs-120 result depends on unmodelled jaw bodies (see domain). A researcher could reuse the ~180-line checker as a teaching toy, not build a paper on it.
evidence.domain: Assembly-by-disassembly with removal directions and a support rule is standard practice. Departure: the gripper is two floating pads with no finger bodies or wrist. A grasp whose jaw axis is parallel to the travel direction puts the leading finger in the part's path; forbidding only those grasps (one-line change in a private copy) drops free/side from 384 to 180 at jaw 30 and 40, while top stays 120. So more than half of the 384 orders, and most of the 'approach direction matters' gap, rest on physically unrealisable grasps; 264 of the 384 side-arm orders also slide parts under an already placed cover. A practitioner would also expect a friction/force-closure or at least contact-area grasp test; none is modelled (stated as a limitation).

defects.what: Grasp model has no jaw/finger bodies: grasps whose jaw axis is parallel to the travel direction are accepted though the leading finger sits in the part's path. Forbidding only those cuts free/side from 384 to 180 (top stays 120), so most of the headline 'approach direction matters: 384 vs 120' gap rests on unrealisable grasps.
No test pins any headline number; four seeded mutations in core logic all survived, two moving the headline 384 to 576 and 204.

Pad negative result misattributed: removing both pad collision checks changes no count, so the grasp model is only a bounding-box width test; 'the pads always find free space' presents an inert model as a finding.

Self-replication question never answered for the design itself: jaw_open is swept freely, but the toy gripper's own fingers open 8 mm (max 12 mm between rails), below the 30 mm its cover needs; the README motivation implies the study answers this.
Result is close to a restatement of the geometry and has no comparison with directional-blocking-graph or ASAP-style planners beyond citation; novelty is minimal (acknowledged in part).
README runtimes stale: ~2 s tests and ~10 s experiments measured at 1.2 s and 1.1 s.

verdict: The numbers are right under the model's stated rules: an independent brute force using a different collision and support method reproduces 384/384/120, the 30 mm threshold, 720/720/120 with gravity off and the pad sweep, and run.py regenerates results.txt exactly. But the model underneath the headline is thinner than the README says. The pads float with no finger bodies, and removing the pad checks changes nothing. Forbidding grasps along the travel axis halves the free/side count to 180. Every seeded bug survived the tests. The self-replication framing is never answered for the gripper's own 8 to 12 mm jaw. Finished as described, but it does not meet the bar for verification, claims, fitness or domain.
